The green-barred woodpecker was formally described in 1788 by the German naturalist Johann Friedrich Gmelin in his revised and expanded edition of Carl Linnaeus's Systema Naturae. C. m. melanolaimus (Malherbe, 1857)
C. m. nigroviridis (Grant, C.H.B., 1911)

The last three subspecies have in the past been separated as the golden-breasted woodpecker (C. melanolaimus), and BirdLife International's Handbook of the Birds of the World (HBW) retains that treatment.[12] The "green-barred" and "golden-breasted" groups interbreed where they meet.[13] Some authors have also treated C. m. nigroviridis as a separate species.[10]
